Nephrotoxic, HTN, gum hypertrophy, hirsutism, tremor
Poor wound healing, mouth ulcers, pneumonitis, ↑lipids
CNIs & sirolimus have a narrow therapeutic index
— trough (C0) levels; watch renal fn, glucose, FBC,
CNIs / sirolimus via CYP3A4 — azoles, macrolides,
CMV, BK polyomavirus (→ nephropathy), PCP, fungal —
Skin SCC and PTLD (EBV-driven B-cell) — reduce
Too much → infection / malignancy; too little →
Tacrolimus and ciclosporin are both nephrotoxic — a rising creatinine may be calcineurin-inhibitor toxicity rather than
rejection; check a trough level before assuming either.
Distinguish the cosmetic clues: ciclosporin causes gum hypertrophy and hirsutism, whereas tacrolimus causes alopecia and is
Sirolimus is not nephrotoxic (useful for CNI-sparing) but impairs wound healing and causes mouth ulcers, pneumonitis and
hyperlipidaemia — a reason to hold it around surgery.
Azathioprine + allopurinol is dangerous: allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase and precipitates severe myelosuppression —
check TPMT and avoid the combination.
OKT3 / muromonab-CD3 is of historical interest only (withdrawn 2010 for cytokine-release syndrome) — modern induction uses
Live vaccines are contraindicated under immunosuppression; and over-immunosuppression trades rejection for infection
Sources: British National Formulary (BNF); British Transplantation Society; KDIGO transplant guidance; StatPearls / LiverTox (muromonab-CD3, withdrawn 2010); EMA Simulect
Doses/targets illustrative & unit-specific: basiliximab 20 mg IV day 0 + day 4; MMF ~1 g BD; CNIs & sirolimus dosed to trough level. Verify locally.
